monument_name: Narakoṭa Four Stone Memorial Pillars (circa 13th-16th cent.)
description_en: The Narakoṭa Pillars date from the 13th to 16th centuries and are now located 200 metres south of the main bazar on the side of the road leading to the village of Narakoṭa. They have been displaced over time, so their current locations and orientations are not the same as they were. They are now arranged in a north-south line.There is no visible decorum on Pillar 001 (JUM0460-001). Pillar 002 (JUM0460-002) is square in shape. It has broken on top. An elongated pike motif can be seen on its south-east facade. The Pillar contains one or two lines of eroded Nāgarī inscription (illegible).The top of Pillar 003 (JUM0460-003) is bulbous. On the south-east side, a pair of circles are engraved. A rosette can be seen inside the left one. Below is a stepped structure (altar?).From the 13th to the 17th centuries, stone memorial pillars were erected throughout the Karnali Basin. They are erected to honour the memory of deceased people, most of whom were warriors (Andolfatto 2019). In Bistabara, there are no inscriptions on the pillars (or any discernible ones). Their typology suggests that they were built between the 13th and 16th centuries.
references: REFERENCES Andolfatto, David C. 2019. Le Pays aux Cent-Vingt-Cinq-Mille Montagnes. Etude Archéologique du Bassin de la Karnali (Népal) entre le XIIe et le XVIe siècle . Paris: Sorbonne Université.
